top_cited_works.title: Enhanced Smoothing Technique for Indirect Optimization of Minimum-Fuel Low-Thrust Trajectories
top_cited_works.venue: Journal of Guidance Control and Dynamics
top_cited_works.abstract: Indirect methods used for solving optimal-control problems, when combined with proper initialization and homotopy approaches, remain attractive for space trajectory optimization, as they are able to achieve fast convergence to a solution of the necessary conditions. In this paper, the extended logarithmic-smoothing technique is revisited and integrated with an indirect method to efficiently generate minimum-fuel time-fixed low-thrust rendezvous trajectories. This approach is considered for three cases, in which equations of motion are expressed in terms of Cartesian, spherical, and modified equinoctial coordinates. In addition, the paper addresses the calculation of the Jacobian matrix of the constraints via an implementation of the state-transition-matrix approach, which avoids the discontinuities of the control along the trajectory. The application of the method to two interplanetary missions from Earth to Mars and to asteroid Dionysus is demonstrated. It is shown that, by exploiting the state transition matrix and the homotopy method, the optimal-control problem becomes amenable to numerical treatment. recent_works.title: Robust Aerocapture Trajectory Optimization Under Atmospheric Density Uncertainty
recent_works.abstract: Aerocapture maneuvers can significantly increase mission design flexibility. Although prior work based on the longitudinal dynamics has established that a bang/bang control profile using bank angle modulation is optimal for minimizing the postaerocapture insertion [Formula: see text], the optimal solution is sensitive to atmospheric uncertainties. This study investigates robust three-degrees-of-freedom (i.e., lateral/longitudinal) aerocapture trajectories under atmospheric density variations. The primer vector theory reveals that the coupled lateral/longitudinal dynamics results in a regularized bang/bang profile. First, using direct collocation, a nonstandard formulation of the desensitized aerocapture problem is developed that reduces the problem dimension using the global sensitivity analysis and enhances numerical accuracy in cost evaluation through state augmentation. The proposed desensitized optimization framework is applied to derive robust trajectories, which maintains a regularized bang/bang profile, with more than one switch in bank angle. recent_works.title: Eigendecomposition parameterization of penalty matrices for enhanced control design: Aerospace applications
WITHDRAWAL: On the Pointing-Constrained Fuel-Optimal Powered Descent Problem
WITHDRAWN: On the Pointing-Constrained Fuel-Optimal Powered Descent Problem
recent_works.abstract: This paper presents theoretical advancements to the three degree-of-freedom (3DOF) powered descent guidance (PDG) problem. A common constraint in the 3DOF PDG problem is the pointing constraint, i.e., an angular limit on the direction of the thrust steering vector constraining it to lie within a cone. New insights are gained into this control-only inequality constraint by analyzing the pointing constraint switching function, whose sign governs its activation. It is shown this constraint will become active at most once on extremals. Moreover, the switch time, should it occur, from active to inactive (or inactive to active) arcs on admissible solutions can be calculated in closed-form. Closed-form solutions to the state and costate ordinary differential equations (including the mass costate) are also derived when this constraint is active. These results can be used to extend fast guidance algorithms based on solving the piecewise algebraic root finding problem, resulting from the necessary conditions of optimality.

recent_works.title: Desensitized Aerocapture Terminal Guidance
recent_works.abstract: In traditional aerocapture terminal guidance, feedback gains are computed with respect to a nominal optimal trajectory determined a priori. In contrast, desensitized aerocapture terminal guidance simultaneously optimizes both the reference trajectory and feedback gains by minimizing sensitivity terms that depend on the feedback gains themselves. Previous studies have demonstrated that aerocapture performance exhibits significant sensitivity to uncertainties in atmospheric density and initial state conditions, particularly initial velocity and flight-path angle. This study develops a desensitized aerocapture terminal guidance approach designed to enhance robustness against dynamic perturbations. The performance and robustness of the desensitized aerocapture terminal guidance is evaluated through Monte Carlo analysis conducted within the Program to Optimize Simulated Trajectories-II (POST2).
